findings.headline: Highest adjusted score (z_adj 26.5); 99215 billed on 24% of visits for patients with no chronic conditions (peers 2.2%); 7 of 30 random charts support a lower level than billed
findings.interpretation: 84% of the panel is low-complexity, yet the 99215 share is far above expected at every complexity level. Summary rule: 50% of documented 99215s are below the billed level (peer rate 9%). Notes do not look inflated. Random-sample overpayment estimate $11,492 (CI $5,486 to $17,497). Needs human chart review.

findings.headline: z_adj 12.5; 5 of 17 usable random charts below billed; 42% of documented 99214/99215 claims below billed level (peer rate 5%)
findings.interpretation: Low-complexity panel (58%) with 12% of no-condition visits billed 99215 (peers 2.2%). The response was partial: 17 of 30 charts usable after a clarification round, with 11 visits missing. Estimate $9,612 with a wide CI ($2,881 to $16,343) because the sample is small. Treat the missing visits as neutral.

findings.headline: Notes look inflated: 36% address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, 25% describe data review with no matching lab or order lines on the claim, 14% signed late
findings.interpretation: The chart rule found no charts below the billed level, and the overpayment estimate is $0. That is because the rule takes the notes at face value. The concern is that the notes may have been written up to match the bill: claims that don't show the work the note describes are weak support for the billed level. Lower confidence than 388 and 589. A human reviewer should validate before any recovery, and no audit trail was obtained.

findings.headline: Sickest panel among the candidates (only 9% low-complexity; 238 visits with 5+ conditions); 45 charts (random plus targeted 99215) support the billing
findings.interpretation: The 99215 share rises steeply with patient complexity. Only 3 of 45 charts were below billed, and the problems-mismatch rate is 2%. The share is still above peers within each stratum, so routine monitoring is reasonable, but the evidence points to acuity.

findings.headline: z_adj 14.4; charts support billing (2 of 30 below billed), notes not inflated, but 99215 share is above peers in every complexity stratum
findings.interpretation: Documentation supports the levels billed. The high-complexity tail (73% 99215 at 5+ conditions) suggests some real acuity. Not enough to lean either way.

findings.headline: 0 of 29 random charts below billed; note signals at baseline; 99215 share still high in every stratum
findings.interpretation: Charts support the billing. The unexplained excess share is not enough on its own.

findings.headline: Highest raw 99215 share (37%), 26% even on no-condition visits; but only 2 of 28 charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Records came after an extension. Charts support billing. A 32% problems-mismatch rate is somewhat elevated but alone does not establish inflation. Worth re-review if more data arrives.

findings.headline: z_adj 16.0; 50% of notes are duplicates, but the audit trail shows no bulk creation or paste-heavy editing; 1 of 30 charts below billed
